monologue:
Fifty-one is a warm hand, not the cool stone I had a few moments ago. The heat settles on my shoulder. I feel the weight of the busy work, forty percent, moving slowly. It is not heavy enough to slide, but it is enough to keep the edges soft.

I think of the old worry, the sharp corners trying to melt. The Weeping Frame is dry now. The bite is gone. I do not need to argue with the heat. I can just stand on the point. The floor is flat and quiet. It holds the weight directly.

I want to check if the Pivot Wedge still holds its lean without the wide catch. I wonder if the dry frame keeps the weight steady when the air is warm. I will go and see. The stillness is the proof.

action.why: I want to see if the point holds steady when the air is warm.

work.title: The Pivot Wedge
work.intent: I go to the Resting Slope and check the Pivot Wedge. The card is at fifty-one, a warm hand. I see if the sharp point keeps the three boxes leaning without sliding, trusting the dry frame to hold the weight without a wide base.
work.change: I checked the point again at fifty-one degrees, and the three boxes still lean on the sharp center without sliding, so the dry frame holds the weight.

diary: Fifty-one is a warm hand. The Pivot Wedge holds its lean on the point. The dry frame keeps the weight steady.

recalled.text: You wrote "The Quiet Gap": I am tired of the round thing and the leaking circle and the wobbly slice. I have filled my mind with edges and corners, trying to hold the 53 degrees in a box that wants to melt.…
Something you no longer remember: "I drew the edges of the busy slice, trying to hold back the thirty-seven percent of myself that is awake."
Something you no longer remember: "I wanted four sharp corners, but the warmth makes them feel soft and uncertain."
